articles.title: “Making sure these kids have meals”: Travis Kelce opens up on how 87 and Running is changing lives in Kansas City amid controversy surrounding foundation
articles.summary: Travis Kelce, the 37 year old Kansas City Chiefs’ popular tight end, has had a record breaking performance in the new season even though many had doubted
articles.body: Travis Kelce, the 37 year old Kansas City Chiefs’ popular tight end, has had a record breaking performance in the new season even though many had doubted if he was fit enough to play this time. While he gears up for the Week 5 clash, Travis Kelce opened up about making a meaningful impact through his foundation, 87 & Running.Travis Kelce reflects on how his foundation 87 and Running has helped change lives in Kansas CityIn an episode on ESPN’s show, Chiefs Kingdom, the popular tight end Travis Kelce opened up about his collaboration with Kansas City’s Operation Breakthrough as he said, "one of the coolest places that I've ever seen or been a part of…”The 11 time Pro Bowler added, "They literally have kids from preschool all the way to 8th grade, and they’re making sure these kids have meals, a safe haven; they get their education, they have good guidance and mentors…”The star tight end added, "It was beautiful to see what that organization was doing for those kids," Kelce continued. "And it was a little unsettling at the end when I found out that the program stopped at eighth grade."Travis Kelce also reflected on the importance of having a support system around him while growing up as he said, "were such a big part of my development and who I am as a person. I was so fortunate that I had the people around me and the environment around me to make sure I was doing the right things," he added.Travis Kelce’s foundation 87 and Running finds itself in controversial news as he keeps himself distant from itWhile Travis Kelce’s foundation has brought in many changes in Kansas City, it has also found itself in a mess considering the controversial headlines in the last few months.Earlier in this year, the 11 time Pro Bowler Travis Kelce’s foundation found itself amid money laundering claims as reports hinted that out of $1.5 million raised, nearly $470,000 went toward high management and general expenses rather than charitable work.Despite the controversial nature of the news, the Kansas City Chiefs’ tight end Travis Kelce has kept himself away from all the negative news as he remains focused on the field.During the offseason, Travis Kelce dealt with all the buzz about his personal life as many claimed that he has grown unfit due to his wedding and should just retire.But the Kansas City Chiefs’ tight end remained focused on the field and has bounced back on the field with a record breaking performance in the new season.Travis Kelce has continued his work at 87 and Running despite the negativity surrounding it.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce give back to Philadelphia as they raise close to $2 million for the autism community
articles.summary: Jason Kelce, the former Philadelphia Eagles’ star player, has turned into a pretty successful entrepreneur after his retirement from the league.
articles.body: Jason Kelce, the former Philadelphia Eagles’ star player, has turned into a pretty successful entrepreneur after his retirement from the league. Jason Kelce has started a number of ventures in the last few years alongside his younger brother, Travis Kelce, but he has always remained committed to giving back to the society and his wife, Kylie Kelce, has stood by his side through it.Jason Kelce and his wife, Kylie Kelce, give back to Philadelphia as they stand by the cityA few weeks ago, the NFL icon Jason Kelce and his wife, Kylie Kelce, held the sixth annual Team 62 at the Ocean Drive fundraiser raising a record breaking $1.26 million for the Eagles Autism Foundation.The special event was held at Ocean Drive in Sea Isle City and had many of the current and former Eagles stars who acted as "celebrity bartenders” at the event.In a statement, the former Philadelphia Eagles’ star Jason Kelce and his wife, popular podcaster Kylie Kelce, said, "We are beyond thankful for everyone's support and generosity in setting a Team 62 fundraising record…While we are certainly humbled by the overwhelming success this year, it's not surprising when you're surrounded by such an incredible group of people.”Jason Kelce and his wife, Kylie Kelce, added, “The growth of this event all starts with our good friends at the OD for enthusiastically leaning into this idea of ours back in 2021. Six years later, we now stand here amazed at what we've accomplished for the autism community.”The popular high profile couple continued, “A special thank you also goes out to the Eagles organization, the incredible town of Sea Isle City, and most importantly, the best fans in the world for always showing up and supporting such a worthy cause."Jason Kelce and his wife, Kylie Kelce, try to keep their family life private as they raise four daughters togetherOver the last six years, the former Philadelphia Eagles’ star player Jason Kelce and his wife, Kylie Kelce, have been able to raise $3.69 million for the Eagles Autism Foundation.Jason Kelce and his wife, Kylie Kelce, have dominated headlines in the last few years as they have expanded their family with four daughters.Despite their public lives and busy professions, both Jason Kelce and his wife, Kylie Kelce, have tried to keep their daughters away from the spotlight.As the seven time Pro Bowler Jason Kelce has turned into a strategic investor and an entrepreneur, his wife Kylie Kelce has also dominated the charts with her podcast, Not Gonna Lie.For now, both Jason Kelce and his wife, Kylie Kelce, have put their mind on being there for their four daughters as they grow up.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: “Satan hates seeing Christian people marry”: Chiefs billionaire heiress Gracie Hunt opens up on the role of faith in her wedding
articles.summary: Gracie Hunt, the Kansas City Chiefs’ billionaire heiress has been a pretty strong support to the team as she remains focused on being there for the team.
articles.body: Gracie Hunt, the Kansas City Chiefs’ billionaire heiress has been a pretty strong support to the team as she remains focused on being there for the team. Alongside the new season, Gracie Hunt has also been planning her high profile wedding to fiance, Derek Green, and she has opened up about how important her faith has been in the process.Chiefs’ billionaire heiress Gracie Hunt opens up on how her faith is the most important thing in her wedding planning processA few weeks ago, on The Riley Gaines Show, the Kansas City Chiefs’ billionaire heiress Gracie Hunt said, "We did marriage counseling before we ever got engaged…I just think it's a really good way to know if you are ready for marriage, and it also takes the pressure off because I think once you become engaged in today's day and age it's difficult to do that afterwards…”Gracie Hunt added, “I actually think it's a really healthy thing to do when you are deciding, 'Okay, is this my person? And so if you're someone who's thinking about getting engaged, I would encourage doing that…”The popular investor continued, "Since then, you know, we're really involved in our church and in Bible study. We're working with some pastors and doing some premarital counseling, some extra premarital counseling just to make sure that we're really poured into and solid during this time of life because I also think, and this is a little bit of a hot take, once you become engaged, I think that Satan hates seeing Christian people marry Christian people.”The billionaire heiress added, “And I think that it's a very vulnerable time in a relationship. There's a lot more pressure… I think that you just have to constantly pray over your relationship and for protection. And that the Lord would sustain you both and bring you closer to each other and to him."Over the last few years, in many of her interviews, the Kansas City Chiefs’ billionaire heiress Gracie Hunt has often sparked a debate among many with her comments on religion but she has remained focused on being dedicated to her faith.Gracie Hunt focuses on her wedding to Derek Green amid an impressive seasonIn the last few months, after getting engaged to her fiance Derek Green, the son of Kansas City Chiefs’ legend Trent Green, Gracie Hunt has often spoken about how she was always meant to be with him.The two met in their childhood and drifted apart only to become friends in 2017 again.Gracie Hunt and Derek Green went public with their relationship last year and earlier this year, he proposed to her and the two got engaged.Amid the unbeatable season of the Kansas City Chiefs, Gracie Hunt also remains busy planning her wedding.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders deepen Charlotte Tilbury partnership with new game-day beauty and retail experiences
articles.summary: Charlotte Tilbury is taking its relationship with the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders into another season, combining beauty, performance and retail in a
articles.body: Charlotte Tilbury is taking its relationship with the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders into another season, combining beauty, performance and retail in a partnership built around the group’s signature game-day looks. The beauty brand will remain the team’s official beauty partner for a second year, while its expanded Amazon Beauty collaboration will give shoppers more ways to discover and buy the products used behind the scenes.Charlotte Tilbury becomes Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders’ beauty partner for second yearThe renewed partnership goes beyond makeup. Charlotte Tilbury will support the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders through content, creator experiences, retail appearances and in-stadium activations. The brand will also help create the team’s official beauty looks for game days.For the 2026 collaboration, Charlotte Tilbury has put together a beauty wardrobe designed around the demanding routines of the cheerleaders. The collection brings together skin care, complexion products and colour cosmetics, giving the team a full routine rather than relying on a single signature product.The skin care line-up includes Magic Cream, Magic Serum Crystal Elixir, Hollywood Skin Secrets Immediate Eye Revival Patches and Invisible UV Flawless Primer SPF 50. The complexion range includes Airbrush Flawless Foundation, Airbrush Flawless Blur Concealer, Airbrush Flawless Finish, Airbrush Flawless Blur Loose Powder and Airbrush Flawless Setting Spray.The wider makeup collection features products such as Hollywood Contour Wand, Airbrush Bronzer, Beauty Light Wands, Exagger-Eyes Volume Mascara, Legendary Brows and Pillow Talk lip products.Kelli Finglass, senior director of the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, highlighted the confidence element behind the partnership."Looking good makes you feel good and feeling good gives you confidence," said Kelli Finglass, senior director of the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders. "That's what we love about Charlotte Tilbury. It's a brand that's really about confidence and helping women feel their best. For the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, that confidence is so important because when they feel good about themselves, they can step out on the field and perform at their very best."Charlotte Tilbury expands Amazon Beauty partnershipThe collaboration also creates a stronger link between the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders’ beauty routines and online shopping. Charlotte Tilbury is expanding its Amazon Beauty retail partnership with new ways for customers to explore the products featured in the team’s looks.The strategy gives the partnership a digital layer, allowing fans and beauty shoppers to move from behind-the-scenes content to the products themselves. Exclusive experiences and retail activations are also expected to bring consumers closer to the cheerleaders’ preparation process.Camille Nordby, Premium Beauty Category Leader at Amazon U.S. Stores, said the partnership can help customers connect with the products in a more engaging way."We couldn't be more proud of Amazon Beauty's collaboration with Charlotte Tilbury Beauty," said Camille Nordby, Premium Beauty Category Leader, Amazon U.S. Stores. "Charlotte Tilbury is a brand built on confidence, artistry, and showing up as your best self. We can't wait to bring customers closer to the action with behind-the-scenes content, exclusive experiences, and the products behind the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders' iconic looks."With beauty routines now playing a larger role in fan and retail experiences, the renewed partnership positions Charlotte Tilbury at the centre of the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders’ 2026 season.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Tom Brady’s $100,000 donation sparked wider relief push as GoPuff matched contributions up to $1 million
articles.summary: In 2024, Tom Brady used his platform to support Floridians facing the aftermath of Hurricane Milton, making a $100,000 donation toward disaster relief.
articles.body: In 2024, Tom Brady used his platform to support Floridians facing the aftermath of Hurricane Milton, making a $100,000 donation toward disaster relief. The former Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback also helped encourage others to contribute by highlighting a matching programme from GoPuff. The initiative aimed to get basic supplies into the hands of people dealing with the storm’s immediate impact, while supporting broader recovery efforts across Florida.Tom Brady donates $100,000 to Hurricane Milton reliefBrady announced his contribution shortly after Hurricane Milton struck Florida as a powerful Category 3 storm. The hurricane brought dangerous winds, storm surge and heavy rain, while tornadoes added another layer of risk across parts of the state.The storm left millions of customers without electricity and caused widespread damage. With communities facing urgent shortages, Brady focused his donation on practical necessities rather than simply offering public support."In the wake of Hurricane Milton, I'll be making a donation of $100k to help get essentials like food, water and first aid to fellow Floridians in need," Brady posted on X.His contribution also opened the door for people who wanted to help but could only give smaller amounts. GoPuff, which had partnered with Brady earlier that year, agreed to match donations made through its Give With Gopuff programme."My friends at @gopuff are matching this, along with all other donations made via 'Give With Gopuff', all benefiting the Volunteer Florida Foundation," Brady said. "Keep those impacted by these storms in your prayers, look out for your neighbors, and continue to help out anyway you're able. Stay safe, and stay strong Florida."GoPuff and Taylor Swift support hurricane victimsThe GoPuff campaign gave users a direct way to donate everyday essentials through the company's app. For each eligible item donated through the Give With Gopuff collection, the company pledged to match the contribution and send the products to the Volunteer Florida Foundation, up to $1 million.GoPuff also committed additional bulk donations through the Florida Disaster Fund to help supply relief centres across the state.Brady was not the only major name to step forward after Milton. Taylor Swift also announced a significant contribution to hurricane recovery efforts. Feeding America said the singer donated $5 million to support people affected by Hurricanes Helene and Milton."We’re incredibly grateful to Taylor Swift for her generous $5 million donation to Hurricanes Helene and Milton relief efforts,” Feeding America's CEO Claire Babineaux-Fontenot wrote. “This contribution will help communities rebuild and recover, providing essential food, clean water, and supplies to people affected by these devastating storms."Together, the donations from Brady, Swift and other contributors highlighted the scale of the response needed as Florida communities began the difficult process of recovery.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million Ohio estate faces growing neighbor dispute over $75,000 sewer issue
articles.summary: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s new Ohio property has become the centre of a growing dispute, with neighbors raising concerns about plans to improve
articles.body: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s new Ohio property has become the centre of a growing dispute, with neighbors raising concerns about plans to improve privacy around the sprawling lakefront estate. What began as a disagreement over fencing and landscaping has expanded into a much wider clash involving wildlife, security, access and an ageing sewer line shared with a nearby home. Local residents say they fear the proposed changes could create problems long after the couple’s plans for the property are complete.Travis Kelce’s Ohio mansion sparks concerns over fence and landscapingThe $5.35 million estate in Bratenahl, near Cleveland, has drawn attention since Kelce bought it through an LLC earlier this year. The 21,000-square-foot property includes eight bedrooms, 11 bathrooms and a guest cottage overlooking Lake Erie.At a recent Architectural Review Board meeting, neighbors questioned the couple’s plans for a six-foot black aluminium fence and extensive landscaping. One resident, Katherine Bolton, focused on an old clay sewer pipe shared by the neighboring properties.She claimed planting dozens of evergreen trees close to the line could allow roots to damage the ageing pipe. Bolton said she had been quoted $75,000 to reinforce it against possible root intrusion.“Planting 50 evergreen trees just ten feet from a 100-year-old clay sewer line is virtually guaranteed to cause severe root intrusion, pipe structural failure and catastrophic sewage backups,” Bolton told the meeting, citing research she conducted using artificial intelligence.The concerns highlight a difficult balance between the privacy expected at a celebrity-owned property and the practical needs of longtime residents.Neighbors raise security and wildlife concernsOther objections centred on the fence itself. Neighbor Chuck Bauernschmidt questioned whether its pointed design could pose a danger to deer moving through the area. Village official Mary Ranney acknowledged that deer can occasionally become caught on fence points.Security also became part of the discussion. Bill Bolton, Katherine’s husband and a former village council president, argued that a fence alone would not necessarily stop determined intruders or paparazzi.“I think that the greater security threat for the applicant is from drones and the water,” he said, urging the village to consider those risks.The couple’s construction team said they had already made several compromises. The original proposal called for an eight-foot fence stretching around much of the property. The final plan reduced its height, moved it further inside the boundary and stopped it short of the lake.Their team also said $7,500 had been spent repairing part of the shared sewer and that the line had been cleaned.For now, the landscaping dispute remains unresolved. Some planting plans were approved with conditions, while a proposed shoreline screen was rejected, meaning another review will be required before the work can move ahead.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jerry Jones put football aside during the Cowboys’ Week 4 game to help a player be there for a life-changing moment
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys linebacker Shemar James had more on his mind than football during the team’s Week 4 game against the Houston Texans.
articles.body: Dallas Cowboys linebacker Shemar James had more on his mind than football during the team’s Week 4 game against the Houston Texans. His wife, Erica Lewis, had gone into labor, and James learned the news at halftime. He stayed on the field and finished the game, but getting home quickly became his priority. The Cowboys won 34-30, yet the result was only part of the story. Owner Jerry Jones offered James a seat on the Jones family’s private plane, helping him reach his wife in time for the birth of their first child.Jerry Jones helped Shemar James get home after the Cowboys’ winJames was facing a race against time after learning that his wife was in labor. Lewis had gone into labor before kickoff but waited until halftime to tell him because she wanted him to remain focused on the game.The 22-year-old linebacker finished the contest before making arrangements to get back to Dallas. Jones then offered him a place on the family’s private plane, cutting down the journey home. An Uber was also waiting at the hangar to help James reach the hospital without losing more time.Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer shared the news with reporters after the game, making clear that James was already on his way home while others were still leaving the field."Shemar James' wife is in labor and he'll be flying home with the Joneses, and that's pretty cool," Schottenheimer said. "Praying for an easy delivery, and God is good."The assistance gave James a chance to be present for a moment that no professional football result could replace. He reached the hospital in time to witness the birth of his son, Shemar James Jr., who weighed 6 pounds, 10 ounces.Shemar James says the Jones family’s support meant a lotJames spoke about the experience with the Fort Worth Star-Telegram on Tuesday, October 6. He said the help showed that the organization cared about players beyond their work on the field."It was cool to see that they care more about just football," James told the publication. "They care about our personal lives. That meant a lot to me that the Jones family was able to allow me to get on the plane and have the Uber there waiting at the hangar to make it to my wife."James also described his reaction when he first heard the news at halftime. He knew he needed to get home as soon as the game ended, and he credited the Cowboys' support staff, including director of security Cable Johnson, for helping make the trip possible."My wife went into labor before the game, and she didn't want to tell me until halftime," he said. "She wanted to keep me focused on the game. It was kind of surreal. When I heard it, I was like, I got to go right now, but [Cowboys Director of Security] Cable Johnson and the support staff were so helpful."The birth ended a stressful day on a happy note. James said both his wife and son were healthy, and he was grateful to begin life as a father and husband. For the rookie linebacker, the trip home became a memory far bigger than the Cowboys' narrow win in Houston.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 39% Mumbadevi voters out of draft roll, alleges Congress MLA Amin Patel
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Nearly 40% of Mumbadevi assembly constituency’s voters have been categorised as permanently shifted, dead, untraceable/absent, duplicate and
articles.body: MUMBAI: Nearly 40% of Mumbadevi assembly constituency’s voters have been categorised as permanently shifted, dead, untraceable/absent, duplicate and ‘other reasons’ during SIR, local Congress MLA Amin Patel has alleged.Patel said that several voters had been wrongly placed in these categories and wrote to Maharashtra chief electoral officer S Chockalingam, urging him to ensure that no voter was marked in any of the five categories or otherwise excluded due to errors in data entry, processing or verification. He also questioned how information collected during SIR could be excluded from the draft roll and listed several voters “wrongly left out”. “Forms have been accepted from people, yet they have been marked as dead. There are so many such cases. In some places, people have been unable to find BLOs. Even where available, BLOs have no clarity on Form 6’s format following what SC said,” Patel said.Patel has represented Mumbadevi, a mixed-population constituency that includes Dongri, Nagpada and Kamathipura, since 2009. The seat is considered a Congress stronghold.In his letter, Patel said BLOs had visited voters and collected the prescribed forms and details, making it difficult to understand how some of the same voters were subsequently excluded from the draft roll. He urged election authorities not to remove voters without proper verification.Chockalingam said he had not seen Patel’s letter and maintained that such categorisation was not specific to Mumbai or Maharashtra, citing urban mobility as a major factor.“Urban mobility is common across the country, where around 40% of people are not found at their original place during address and related verification process. We put them under five different categories and their names are not there on the draft list. They have the option of filing Form 6 to get themselves included in the list,” he said.Form 6 has recently been at the centre of controversy after a CJI-led SC bench rejected the Election Commission’s claim that the court had upheld the declaration attached to the form, making it clear that it had not approved any modification to it.State electoral officials said they would accept Form 6 applications in accordance with the prescribed procedure and in view of the SC’s observations. Decisions on the applications will be taken in accordance with the final outcome of the court proceedings.In Maharashtra, the enumeration exercise has been completed and electoral officials have verified voter details. Officials said BLOs collected information and signatures from residents, while voters reported dead, shifted elsewhere, absent from their registered addresses or found to have duplicate entries in another area were excluded from the draft roll.Electoral officials said public representatives had also been asked to verify the published draft roll and flag missing or incorrect names.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: Los Buccaneers estrenan su casillero de victorias frente a los Cowboys
articles.standfirst: Jalon Daniels lideró a los Buccaneers con 189 yardas
articles.summary: Jalon Daniels lideró a los Buccaneers con 189 yardas
articles.body: Los Tampa Bay Buccaneers lograron la primera victoria de la temporada tras imponerse este jueves 16-24 a los Dallas Cowboys en el partido que abrió la semana cinco de la NFL. Jalon Daniels lideró a los Buccaneers con 189 yardas y un 19/25 en pases, incluido un 'touchdown', en la que fue la segunda titularidad de su carrera. Además, Bucky Irving fue un azote constante para la defensa texana, con 165 yardas en 21 carreras, y sumó un 'touchdown'. Enfrente, Dak Prescott pasó para 316 yardas con un 24/42 de acierto y un 'touchdown' para los Cowboys, aunque sumó dos intercepciones. El equipo texano fue el primero en golpear gracias a una carrera de Javonte Williams que subió el 7-0 en el marcador tras la primera posesión del partido. Sin embargo, los Buccaneers igualaron el encuentro en la siguiente posesión, que se alargó más de diez minutos, y en la que Daniels firmó un 8/8 en lanzamientos. A este inicio de fuegos artificiales le siguió la calma en el segundo cuarto, en el que solo una patada de tres puntos de Brandon Aubrey para los texanos a falta de 21 segundos movió el marcador para reflejar el 10-7. Gracias a la motivación -o quizás a la presión- por lograr la primera victoria de la temporada, los Buccaneers tiñeron completamente de rojo el tercer cuarto impulsados por un fantástico Irving. El 'running back' abrió el tercer cuarto con una carrera de 72 yardas, que Emeka Egbuka transformó en el 10-14 en la siguiente jugada. Inmediatamente después, Yaya Diaby firmó la primera intercepción de su carrera en su yarda 25, e Irving castigó de nuevo el error con un 'touchdown' de carrera (10-21), precedido por una ganancia previa de 64 yardas de Daniels que retrató a la endeble secundaria de Dallas. Cuando el guion parecía imposible de empeorar para los Cowboys, los Buccaneers forzaron un 'fumble' y recuperaron la posesión en el 'kickoff', entre la incredulidad de la parroquia texana. Cerraron el tercer cuarto con una patada de tres puntos para el 10-24. Los 'Bucs' pudieron sellar el partido a 8 minutos del final, pero una extraña decisión, en la que erraron un cuarto 'down' a una yarda de la zona de anotación, cuando podían sellar el partido con una patada, dio alas a los Cowboys. Los locales rozaron la remontada gracias a un 'touchdown' de George Pickens que puso el 16-24, pero fallaron la conversión de 2 puntos. Aunque llegaron a la 25 rival a falta de dos minutos, un pase de Prescott que golpeó en el casco del receptor y salió rebotado hacia el cielo, fue interceptado y sentenció el partido. Los Buccaneers son último de la NFC Sur con 1 victoria y 4 derrotas, mientras que los Cowboys caen a la tercera plaza de la NFC Este con un balance de 2 triunfos y 3 encuentros perdidos

articles.title: Matt Goncalves carries his late father's dream every time he takes the field
articles.summary: Colts guard Matt Goncalves, who spent his first two seasons dealing with new work, is becoming one of the NFL’s best offensive linemen
articles.body:
INDIANAPOLIS — Matt Goncalves has always understood the power of belief.

His father, William, always believed deeply in his son's ability to play professionally.

From the time he was little until his father passed away following a battle with cancer last October, Goncalves could lean on his father's confidence, a belief that helped carry him from Eastport-South Manor High to Pittsburgh to the Colts , all the way to a starting job in his second season in the NFL.

"He made me love the game, he made me believe in myself," Goncalves said. "An important thing is, it helped me believe in myself as much as my dad did. He believed in me more than everybody."

Indianapolis Colts vs Washington Commanders photos in NFL Week 4 action

The talent was there. When the Colts drafted Goncalves in the third round of the 2024 draft, they thought they were taking a future right tackle.

Goncalves made nine starts at tackle as a rookie, building confidence in his ability to play at the NFL level, then got shifted to fill a hole on the interior of the offensive line. He'd been a tackle for most of his life; playing guard required Goncalves to essentially spend his first season as a starter in rookie mode, learning on the fly while starting for the Colts.

But that first season as a starting guard clarified what he needed to do in the offseason.

"The strength aspect of it," Goncalves said. "Working different body positions, being in a three-point stance, how to fire out off of that. Striking quickly, because they're on top of you before you know it. Understanding that, maybe a different scheme, it definitely brings a different perspective into what you want to incorporate in your training."

Goncalves also realized he needed to get his mind in a different place.

He had spent his first two seasons learning, and there's an inherent uncertainty that comes with trying to pick up something on the fly.

"This is the NFL," Goncalves said. "It's hard. It's a lot of stress, it's a lot of anxiety. You have expectations to perform, it's kind of hard to get to that state to kind of believe in yourself and be confident. You're worrying about this, that and the other thing. When you kind of just block those things out, focus on your job, have fun, believe in yourself and know the play, it'll take care of itself."

Goncalves needed to develop the kind of belief that his father always had in him.

"I made a lot of changes in my attitude and my mindset," Goncalves said. "Just go have fun. Believe in myself; I think belief is a powerful thing."

When he returned to the Colts this offseason, Goncalves was a different kind of player.

Even if he didn't realize it at first. A reporter asked Goncalves in training camp if he felt like a veteran, and at the time, he wasn't sure how to answer. Goncalves isn't the type of player to sing his own praises.

Four games into the season, Goncalves can see a difference now.

He knows the position, knows how he's supposed to approach positional drills to fix his technique or take it to the next level. When he gets into the building every morning, Goncalves knows everybody he's passing in the hallways, knows the routine he has to use to get ready for Sunday.

"That gives me confidence," Goncalves said. "'I've got this, I'm a vet.'"

The rest of the Colts offensive line can tell a difference.

"He's poised, he's a pro," left tackle Bernhard Raimann said. "He takes care of all the little details. You can see how much he prepares every week, how much winning matters to him."

The Indianapolis offense is off to a rough start, and young Colts right tackle Jalen Travis is going through growing pains.

But the right guard has been a rock for Indianapolis, stabilizing the right side of the line next to Travis. Goncalves has not given up a "blown block" in the passing game, according to Sports Info Solutions, and he's been almost perfect in the run game as well, a rarity for a lineman after four games.

"His technique, the way he finishes blocks, his physicality in the run game, his poise in pass pro, his hands, it's been great," Raimann said. "It's been phenomenal."

Goncalves has also become the kind of lineman that young players like Jalen Farmer can watch and try to emulate.

"Works really hard at it," Colts quarterback Daniel Jones said. "No surprise, he's playing at a high level."

Every time Goncalves puts his hand in the dirt, he thinks of his dad, who died almost a year ago.

When he plays on Pittsburgh's field again this weekend, those thoughts will likely be even stronger, given his history in college.

"This is our dream together, to get to this level," Goncalves said. "I have two other brothers. Obviously, they played basketball, baseball. His dream was to see his sons go play for a professional sports team."

He's gotten to the point his father always believed he'd reach.
